subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should sensitive keys explicitly configured in `skills.entries.<skill>.env` be admitted into host exec broadly, or only through a scoped skill/plugin-owned execution path?
rationale: The reported availability regression is source-backed, but the obvious broad allow changes which child processes can receive secrets and overlaps the open generic-exec secret-leak issue.

options.title: Design scoped credential delivery
options.body: Preserve the skill env contract by delivering credentials only to intended skill-owned execution paths and stripping them from unrelated generic exec children.

options.title: Allow explicit env broadly
options.body: Treat operator-configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as consent for all admitted sensitive names to reach host exec during that run, with dangerous host names still blocked.

options.title: Patch gog metadata narrowly
options.body: Declare `GOG_ACCOUNT` and `GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD` for the bundled gog skill while leaving arbitrary sensitive configured keys blocked.

recommendation.title: Design scoped credential delivery
recommendation.body: Preserve the skill env contract by delivering credentials only to intended skill-owned execution paths and stripping them from unrelated generic exec children.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sits on the SecretRef and host exec env security boundary where this person has the strongest recent history.
